battle.name: 潼關、南京之戰
battle.brief: 金宣宗貞祐四年（1216），成吉思汗命蒙古將領三摸合拔都率萬騎由西夏取道關陝，襲破潼關，東進至黃河南岸窺金新都南京（汴京），見金軍屯重兵遂渡河北歸，潼關旋為金軍收復。此役是蒙古配重式回回砲投入關中攻關的開始，卡面配重投石車的長臂配重即屬此類機械。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 1216年的潼關、南京之戰，是蒙古帝國與金朝在關陝至河南這條縱深上的第一次正面進攻，交戰雙方的組織形態差異很大。蒙古一方以成吉思汗的大汗本部為核心，軍隊按十戶、百戶、千戶編制，怯薛近衛護衛大汗營帳，作戰的基本單位是騎兵小組；此時蒙古已把草原兵制與漢地降軍分開，漢人降軍多用於攻城、運糧與營造，蒙古騎兵則負責野戰與追擊。此次西進的一支萬騎由西夏方向進入關陝，領兵的是蒙古將領三摸合拔都，屬於成吉思汗對金作戰的第二次大規模派兵，第一次便是1215年攻潼關受阻。金朝一方在宣宗南遷汴京之後，以南京（汴京）為新都，樞密院與都統府調度各路，軍隊仍以女真、契丹、漢地三種人丁組成的猛安謀克為骨幹，漢地州縣徵發的步卒與匠戶編成的守城部隊佔多數；潼關由西面統軍司與關陝招討司一線防守，關外沿黃河南岸設有前哨堡寨，河南、山東、河北的屯兵名義上仍歸朝廷節制，實際上河北已失、山東有紅袄軍起義在牽制，糧道與兵源都不穩。戰線之外的西夏被迫讓蒙古軍借道關陝，南宋則在金廷遣使求援時議而不決，只備糧餉而不出兵。金廷內部也分成主戰與主逃兩派，遷都之議屢屢被提起，整體指揮缺乏統一的方針，這是守方在潼關與南京兩地屢屢失機的體制原因。
countriesEn: The campaign of Tong Pass and Nanjing in 1216 was the first serious Mongol advance against Jin along the line running from the passes of Shaanxi down into Henan, and the two sides were organised in very different ways. On the Mongol side the core was the Great Khan's own host under Chinggis Khan, the army arranged in tens, hundreds and thousands of men, with the keshig guard keeping watch around the great tent; the tactical unit was a mounted group. By this time the Mongols had already separated the steppe troops from the Chinese troops they had enrolled: the Chinese were used for siege work, for transport and for construction, while Mongol cavalry remained the arm of the field battle and of the pursuit. The column that came west in this campaign entered from Western Xia with a leader, the Mongol commander San Moghabdudu, and formed part of the Great Khan's second large dispatch against Jin, the first having been the attempt on Tong Pass in 1215 that failed. On the Jin side, after the Xuanzong had moved south to Bianjing, the new capital at Nanjing was governed by the Privy Council and the Directorate of Commanders, and the army still rested on the meng'an and mouke made up of Jurchen, Khitan and Chinese blood, with the greater part of the men being levies from the Chinese prefectures and workmen from the towns turned into garrison troops. Tong Pass was held by the western command and the circuit recruiting office of Shaanxi, with outposts strung along the south bank of the Yellow River, and the garrisons of Henan, Shandong and Hebei were nominally at the court's disposal, though Hebei was already lost, Shandong was being torn by the Red Coat rising, and neither the supply line nor the recruitment was secure. Outside the line, Western Xia was compelled to let the Mongol army pass through its territory, and when Jin envoys came asking the Southern Song for help, the Song court debated and did not act: it provided grain but no troops. The Jin court was itself split between those who would fight and those who would run, the question of moving the capital again was raised more than once, and there was no single plan of command. That, in the end, is why the defenders kept missing their chances at both Tong Pass and Nanjing.
people: 成吉思汗是這一戰線的決策者。1215年蒙古軍攻破金中都之後，他沒有立刻揮師直趨汴京，而是先在漠北與西夏周旋，把對金作戰的主責交給木華黎；1216年他親征西夏，同時派三摸合拔都率萬騎自西夏取道關陝，襲取潼關，目的正如後人記述的那樣，是「以略河南」，用一支可以抽走的騎兵去探金朝新都周邊的虛實，而不是立即攻城。木華黎在這幾年裡以漢地降軍與蒙古本部兵混編，替蒙古處理漢地的徵發與屯駐，他的部眾曾一再打到真定、太原一帶，把金朝的注意力往北方拉扯。金宣宗完顏允恭是守方的最高決策者，他南遷汴京之後面對的是一個兩難：河北之地已失，潼關是通往關中的唯一門戶，若再失潼關，中都與西京方向再無屏障；但若集中兵力救援潼關，汴京本身又會空虛。潼關的守將與西面統軍司的指揮在《金史》裏只留下職銜而少有名字，這恰恰說明此役在金廷檔案中的份量：它是一場被記錄下來、卻沒有被徹底交代的敗仗。參戰者方面，最值得記住的是那些沒有留下名字的兵卒：蒙古的萬騎是從漠北臨時徵發的部族騎兵，靠馬匹與隨軍馬群自備口糧；金的守軍則是關城內外的屯軍與從河南各州縣調來的步卒，兩軍的差別最終體現在誰能在關外的黃河灘上撐住一場真正的攻城戰。
peopleEn: Chinggis Khan was the man who decided this front. After the Mongols carried the Jin capital of Zhongdu in 1215 he did not march straight on Bianjing; he spent his time in the steppe and against Western Xia and handed the main responsibility for the war against Jin to Muqali. In 1216, while he campaigned in person against Western Xia, he sent San Moghabdudu with ten thousand horsemen by way of Western Xia and the passes of Shaanxi to strike at Tong Pass, for the purpose, as later chroniclers put it, of a raid to test the lands south of the river: a body of cavalry that could be withdrawn again, sent out to see what strength the new Jin capital had around it, not to besiege it. In these years Muqali mixed Chinese surrendered troops with his own Mongol units and used them to handle the levying and the billeting of the Chinese lands; his men pushed as far as Zhending and Taiyuan again and again, pulling the Jin's attention northward. The Xuanzong of Jin, Wanyan Yungong, was the supreme decision-maker on the defending side, and after the move south to Bianjing he was caught in a dilemma: the territory north of the capital was gone, Tong Pass was the one gate into Guanzhong, and if that too fell there would be no screen left towards the former capitals; but if the troops were concentrated to relieve Tong Pass, Bianjing itself would be left hollow. The defenders of Tong Pass and the officers of the western command are left in the History of Jin as little more than titles, with few names, and that is precisely what the weight of this campaign was in the Jin archives: a defeat that was recorded but never fully accounted for. Among the participants, the men who left no names deserve the closest attention: the ten thousand horsemen were clan cavalry levied in the steppe, living off their horses and the herds that marched with them, while the Jin garrison was made up of the men quartered in the pass and of foot soldiers drawn from the prefectures and counties of Henan. The difference between the two armies came down, in the end, to which of them could hold a real siege on the sandbanks of the Yellow River outside the pass.
kits: 卡面這件配重投石車是十二世紀歐洲的成熟形制：一根長臂，一端掛著裝石彈的皮兜，另一端用槓桿吊起配重石，兩端同時下落時把石彈甩過城牆，射程與破壞力都遠勝靠人力拉索的中國拋石機。同一機制的拋石機在蒙古軍中有個漢語名稱，叫回回炮，一般認為由西域回回的工程師在十二世紀末至十三世紀初帶入蒙古軍中，《金史》記1212至1213年涿州、1214至1215年中都兩役中蒙古攻城已用回回炮，1216年成吉思汗又把攻城用的砲石與工匠正式編為專門的砲軍，明確以「砲石為先」。潼關一役是這支部隊第一次在關中攻關。這條戰線上的其他器械同樣值得記錄：蒙古軍用過雲梯、搭城一類的攻城車、撞竿以及填壕的土木器材，攻守雙方也都用過從中都與河北繳獲的漢地攻城器械；金守軍的裝備則以弓弩為主，關城上架有硬弓與神臂弓一類的強弓，另有震天雷、毒火箭與火藥箭等爆裂與燃燒兵器，木製拒馬與鹿角佈在城門與坡道之間，牆面則以磚石包砌加固。運輸與後勤同樣是裝備的一部分：蒙古騎兵靠馬群馱載，攻城用的石彈、砲架的木料與填壕的柴土都要靠牛車和役畜運到砲位；金軍的糧秣則靠汴河水運與河南各縣的徵發，潼關關城本身儲糧有限，一旦關外被封住，關內守軍的處境立刻惡化。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the mature form of the European counterweight trebuchet of the twelfth century: a long arm, with a sling holding the stone at one end and a counterweight hung on a lever at the other, both ends falling together so that the stone is hurled over the wall, giving both range and destructive power far beyond the traction trebuchets worked by manpower in China. A throwing engine of the same mechanism had a Chinese name in the Mongol army, the huihui pao, and it is generally held that engineers of the Muslim communities of the west brought it to the Mongols in the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries; the History of Jin records the huihui pao in Mongol sieges of Zhuozhou in 1212 and 1213 and of Zhongdu in 1214 and 1215, and in 1216 Chinggis Khan formed the stones and the craftsmen for the assault into a dedicated artillery corps and made it plain that the stones came first. The battle of Tong Pass was the first time that corps went into action at a pass in Guanzhong. The other machines on this front deserve their own record: the Mongols used scaling ladders, siege towers of the tower type, battering rams and timber for filling the ditches, and both sides used Han siege equipment captured at Zhongdu and in Hebei; the Jin defenders relied above all on bows and crossbows, with heavy bows and the arm-braced crossbow mounted on the walls, together with the thunder-crash bomb, poisoned fire arrows and gunpowder arrows, with wooden cheval-de-frise and antler obstacles set before the gates and the road up, and the wall faces revetted in brick and stone. Transport and supply were part of the equipment as well: the Mongol cavalry carried its loads on the horses, and the stones for the engines, the timber for the frames and the brushwood for the ditches had to be hauled to the emplacements by ox carts and draught animals; the Jin drew its grain from the water transport of the Bian canal and from the levies of the counties of Henan, and the pass itself stored little food, so that once the outside was shut off the condition of the garrison inside turned bad at once.
tactics: 蒙古的戰法在這條戰線上有清楚的三層。第一層是騎兵的縱深與速度：萬騎不打算在關前久屯，而是以數百騎為一隊在黃河南岸與關北山道之間反覆切換，試圖切斷關城與洛陽、華州一線的聯絡，逼金軍分兵。第二層是攻城器械的定向使用：潼關建在崤山與秦嶺之間的夾縫裏，黃河在北面貼著城牆流過，關城東西長約一千五百米，牆高數丈，可供架砲的地面極其有限，配重式拋石車因此只能架在關北河灘或關外西南的開闊處，用長臂越過城頭去打城牆上部的守軍與城門樓，而不是像平原地攻城那樣把整面牆掀開；石彈從高處落下，摧毀的是城頭的射孔、旗幟與密集的守軍。第三層是撤退的乾淨：見金軍在汴京一線屯有重兵，蒙古軍不戀戰，渡黃河北歸，把這次行動做成一次偵察而不是一次攻佔。金的守方則完全依靠地形：把主力放在關城內與城下的塹壕中，弓弩居高臨下封鎖坡道，砲與火藥武器在城頭對付靠近的攻城部隊，蒙古攻城者一旦進入坡道射程之內便難以兼顧防護與載具；守軍又在蒙古退走之後收復失守的關城與城外的堡寨，重新把西線的大門堵上。守方的弱點不在城牆而在指揮：援軍如何調度、要不要出關野戰、何時撤回汴京，各方意見不一，戰機因此一再錯過。
tacticsEn: The Mongol method on this front had three clear layers. The first was the depth and the speed of the cavalry: the ten thousand horsemen had no intention of lying long before the pass, but worked in bands of several hundred between the south bank of the Yellow River and the mountain tracks north of the pass, trying to cut the pass off from Luoyang and Huazhou and to force the Jin to divide. The second was the aimed use of the siege engines: Tong Pass is built in the cleft between the Xiao Mountains and the Qinling, the Yellow River runs hard against the wall on the north, the walled town runs about one thousand five hundred metres from east to west with a wall several fathoms high, and the ground on which an engine can stand is extremely limited. The counterweight trebuchet could therefore only be emplaced on the sandbanks north of the pass or in the open ground to the south-west outside it, throwing its long arm over the head of the wall to strike at the defenders on the wall-top and at the gate towers, rather than battering down an entire face of wall as could be done in flat country; the stones falling from that height destroyed the loopholes, the banners and the crowded ranks of the garrison. The third was the cleanliness of the withdrawal: finding the Jin heavily entrenched on the Bianjing line, the Mongols did not press the attack, crossed the Yellow River and went north, turning the whole operation into a reconnaissance rather than an occupation. The Jin defence, by contrast, leaned entirely on the ground: the main body was posted inside the walls and in the ditches below them, bows and crossbows commanding the road up from the heights, cannons and gunpowder weapons on the wall-top dealing with the assault troops as they came close, and once the Mongols entered the range of the uphill fire they could not keep both their protection and their vehicles. After the Mongols withdrew the garrison retook the fallen town and the outposts outside it and closed the western gate again. The weakness of the defenders lay not in the wall but in the command: how the relieving troops were to be moved, whether to give battle in the open or to hold the pass, and when to fall back on Bianjing were all disputed, and the chance was missed again and again.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間：金宣宗貞祐四年（1216），蒙古軍自西夏取道關陝攻潼關；前一年（1215）蒙古已有一次攻潼關失利，同年金中都亦陷落；1217年起蒙古命木華黎總領漢地軍事，這場戰役是1215至1218年間蒙古對金一系列試探中最烈的一回。兵力：西進的蒙古先鋒記作「萬騎」，即一萬名騎兵，數量不多但全是能戰的騎兵；金方潼關守軍與前哨的具體數目不見記載，可以確定的是南京（汴京）一線屯有重兵，而這一點正是蒙古沒有深進的原因。地理：潼關在今陝西渭南市潼關縣，東倚崤山、西臨黃河、南接秦嶺，關城東西長約一千五百米，牆高數丈，是一夫當關的地形；關距西安約一百二十公里，距靈寶約四十公里，至金新都南京（汴京）直線不足四百公里，騎兵行軍每日可及百餘里。損失：雙方陣亡數目各史無明載，潼關一度失守而旋為金軍收復，故雙方都沒有可報的殘滅性損失，這也是此役在戰史中長期被視為一次試探而非決戰的原因。物資：萬騎隨軍馬群的口糧、攻城石彈、砲架木料與填壕柴土都要就地取用或由後方運來；金的糧秣靠汴河水運與河南徵發，河北已失、山東有事，南京的存量決定了金廷能守多久。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. In time: in the fourth year of the Zhenyou era of the Xuanzong of Jin (1216) the Mongol army came by way of Western Xia and the Shaanxi passes to attack Tong Pass; in the year before (1215) the Mongols had already made one attempt on Tong Pass and had been repulsed, and in the same year the Jin capital of Zhongdu fell; from 1217 the Mongols entrusted Muqali with the direction of the war in the Chinese lands, and this campaign was the fiercest of the series of Mongol probes against Jin between 1215 and 1218. In strength: the Mongol vanguard that came west is recorded as ten thousand horsemen, a force not large but composed entirely of fighting cavalry; the exact numbers of the Jin garrison at Tong Pass and of the outposts are not recorded, while what can be established is that the line at Nanjing (Bianjing) was held in strength, and that is the reason the Mongols did not press on. In geography: Tong Pass stands in what is now Tongguan county of Weinan, Shaanxi, with the Xiao Mountains to the east, the Yellow River to the west and the Qinling to the south; the walled town runs about one thousand five hundred metres from east to west with a wall several fathoms high, and the ground is that of a place one man can hold against an army. The pass is about one hundred and twenty kilometres from Xi'an, about forty from Lingbao, and less than four hundred in a straight line from the new Jin capital at Nanjing (Bianjing), while a mounted column can cover more than a hundred li a day. In losses: no source gives the numbers of dead on either side; Tong Pass fell for a time and was then retaken by the Jin, so neither side could report a ruinous loss, and that too is why this campaign has long been read as a probe rather than a decisive battle. In stores: the rations of ten thousand horsemen, the stones for the engines, the timber for the frames and the brushwood for the ditches all had to be taken on the spot or brought up from behind; the Jin drew grain from the water route of the Bian canal and from the levies of Henan, and with Hebei lost and Shandong in disorder, the stores at Nanjing determined how long the court could hold out.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因有遠近兩層。遠的一層是蒙古對金的戰爭本身：金朝多年對漠北草原既分化又索取，把蒙古部眾當作可以驅使的附庸，1211年成吉思汗斷絕進貢、起兵南下，1212至1215年先取涿州、再圍中都，金宣宗被迫南遷汴京。蒙古在失去中都以後並不急著強攻一座守備完整的新都，而是要先掃清西面的障礙。潼關正是這樣的障礙：它一夫當關，控著關中通向河南的孔道，卡住它，蒙古的騎兵才有可能在關陝與河南之間自由機動。近的一層是1216年的具體算盤：成吉思汗正在西征西夏，關中與西夏之地近在手邊，順手派一支萬騎越關試探，既可偵察南京周邊的兵力，又可試探潼關守備的虛實；金廷內部則因河北喪失、山東紅袄軍起義與朝堂上的南遷之議而人心浮動，潼關在上年已被蒙古攻過一次而未失，正好使金廷把這一線視為次要方向，防守因而偏鬆。於是一支並不打算攻城的騎兵，遇上了一段沒有被重兵填滿的關防，這場戰爭就這樣打起來了。
causeEn: The war had a near cause and a far one. The far one is the Mongol war against Jin itself: for years the Jin court had used division and extraction against the steppe, treating the Mongol clans as subjects that could be driven at will; in 1211 Chinggis Khan cut off the tribute and rose in the south, took Zhuozhou in 1212 and 1213, sat down before Zhongdu from 1214, and forced the Xuanzong to move south to Bianjing. Having taken Zhongdu, the Mongols were in no hurry to assault a fully defended new capital; they wanted first to clear the obstacles on their western side. Tong Pass was such an obstacle: it is a place one man can hold, and it commands the only corridor from Guanzhong into Henan. Until it was sealed, the Mongol cavalry could not manoeuvre freely between Shaanxi and Henan. The near cause is the arithmetic of 1216: Chinggis Khan was in the field against Western Xia with Guanzhong and the Xia lands close at hand, so he sent a body of ten thousand horsemen over the pass by the cheapest route, both to see what strength was gathered around Nanjing and to test how thin the defence of Tong Pass had grown. On the Jin side the court was unsettled by the loss of Hebei, by the Red Coat rising in Shandong and by the debate in the council over moving the capital again; Tong Pass had been attacked by the Mongols the year before and had held, which led the Jin court to treat that direction as secondary, and the defence there was left thin. So a body of cavalry that had no intention of besieging anything met a line of forts that was not filled with heavy troops, and that is how this war was fought.
impact: 這次進攻本身沒有改變中原的歸屬，卻改變了兩邊的打算。對蒙古來說，1216年的收穫是情報：金朝的新都仍有重兵，強攻汴京的代價太高，於是成吉思汗在1217年改弦更張，命木華黎總領漢地軍事，以漢軍降將、漢地糧秣與工匠替蒙古辦事，蒙古的攻勢由掠奪轉向有組織的征服，這一轉變正是從潼關、汴京一線的偵察開始。對金朝來說，收穫是教訓與恐慌：潼關這樣的地形竟被一次輕騎突進攻破，說明西線的守備只靠城牆而不靠預備隊；於是金廷在潼關與黃河沿線重加兵、增修城壘、補充砲位，同時把遷都與求援的討論提上日程，遣使向南宋求援。南宋沒有出兵，只備了糧餉，但此舉本身已說明中原的處境。此後的走向也由此鋪開：1227年成吉思汗提出借道南宋迂回攻金的策略，1230年以後拖雷部再攻潼關，1232年潼關失守，汴京隨之淪陷，金哀宗退保蔡州，1234年金朝滅亡。兵器史上，這場戰役是配重式拋石機這條技術線在關中的一次早期實戰記錄：蒙古的砲軍第一次在有要塞可依的關隘攻城中成建制地使用砲石，配重長臂把石彈越過城頭落進關內的辦法，後來在十三世紀末的襄陽、樊城攻防中被推到極限，那時一發石彈足以擊碎城樓、壓死守軍。一件兵器由歐洲傳入草原技術體系、再落到中國的關城之下，往往要經過這樣一次試探才會被真正制度化。
impactEn: This attack changed no ownership in the Central Plain, but it changed what both sides intended to do. For the Mongols the profit of 1216 was intelligence: the new Jin capital was still held in strength and the cost of assaulting Bianjing directly was too high, so in 1217 Chinggis Khan changed his arrangements and set Muqali over the war in the Chinese lands, putting Chinese surrendered commanders, Chinese grain and Chinese craftsmen to work for the Mongols, and the Mongol offensive turned from plunder to organised conquest; that turn began with the reconnaissance of the Tong Pass and Bianjing line. For the Jin the profit was a lesson and a fright: a position like Tong Pass had been carried by a single cavalry thrust, which showed that the western line was defended by walls alone and by no reserve; the court accordingly reinforced Tong Pass and the Yellow River line, repaired the fortifications, added gun positions, and at the same time put the question of moving the capital and of asking for help onto the table and sent envoys to the Southern Song. The Song sent no troops and provided grain only, but the fact that it was asked at all showed how bad the position of the Central Plain had become. The course of later events was laid out from that point: in 1227 Chinggis Khan proposed to borrow the road through the Southern Song in order to turn the war on Jin; after 1230 Tolui's host attacked Tong Pass again; in 1232 the pass fell and Bianjing was carried soon after; the Aizong of Jin fell back on Caizhou, and in 1234 the Jin dynasty ended. In the history of weapons this campaign is an early practical record of the counterweight trebuchet line in Guanzhong: the Mongol artillery corps used stones as an organised arm for the first time in an assault on a fortified pass, and the trick of hurling the stone over the head of the wall into the pass was carried to its limit in the sieges of Xiangyang and Fancheng at the end of the thirteenth century, where a single stone could shatter a tower and kill the men beneath it. A weapon that travels from Europe into the steppe's technical system and then falls upon a Chinese fort below the pass generally has to pass through a probe like this one before it is truly institutionalised.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有得到想要的東西，勝負的走向此後才慢慢顯形。蒙古軍破潼關之後東進，在黃河南岸一帶窺見南京城郊的金軍屯列，判斷強攻新都的代價太高，遂渡黃河北還，關外的堡寨與關城也陸續為金軍收復，潼關仍在金朝手中。對金朝而言，國祚未斷，南京未陷，但它失去的是西線的主動：此後潼關一線長期處在蒙古的陰影之下，直到1230年代再被大軍包圍。對蒙古而言，一次沒有佔領的偵察換來了更珍貴的東西——一套可以複製的攻城方法與一批可以徵用的漢地工匠，這些東西在1217年之後被編入木華黎的軍令系統，最終在1230年代把金朝推向滅亡。回頭看配重投石車在這場戰役中的位置：它大概是以回回炮的名義出現在潼關外的灘地上，長臂越過城頭，把石彈丟進關內的守軍陣中；一次攻不下的關城因此可以用砲石慢慢去啃，但關隘的地形也同樣限制了砲位，限制了配重臂展開的空間，限制了射程。工程與地形互相牽制的道理，就在潼關這一段河谷裡被演示了一次。
resultEn: In the end neither side got what it wanted, and the direction of the war only became clear later. After carrying Tong Pass the Mongols advanced east, saw on the south bank of the Yellow River the columns the Jin had drawn up before the capital at Nanjing, judged that a direct assault on the new capital would cost too much, and crossed the Yellow River and went north; the outposts outside the pass and the town itself were retaken one by one by the Jin, and Tong Pass remained in Jin hands. For the Jin the dynasty was not broken and the capital was not taken, but the initiative on the western line was lost: the Tong Pass line stood under the Mongol shadow for years afterwards, until it was surrounded by a great army in the 1230s. For the Mongols a reconnaissance that occupied nothing bought something far more valuable, a method of siege that could be copied and a body of Chinese craftsmen that could be conscripted; after 1217 these were brought into Muqali's command system, and in the 1230s they pushed the Jin towards destruction. Looking back at the place of the counterweight trebuchet in this campaign: it stood, most likely, on the sandbanks outside Tong Pass under the name of the huihui pao, its long arm reaching over the head of the wall to drop stones into the ranks of the garrison within; a pass that could not be taken in one rush could thus be gnawed away with stones. But the terrain of a pass limited the emplacements just as much, limiting the space in which the counterweighted arm could swing and limiting the range. The way in which engineering and terrain pull against each other was demonstrated once, in that stretch of the Yellow River valley at Tong Pass.
